content.value_statement: Teams often need consistent feedback on readability, naming, and code organization. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical checklist for everyday code quality review.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews for naming, function design, organization, comments, and documentation.
Flags common issues such as magic numbers, unclear names, deep nesting, and large functions.
Applies SOLID review questions to classes, interfaces, dependencies, and extension points.
Provides Socratic questions for coaching junior developers during review.
Supplies naming conventions for variables, constants, functions, classes, and files.
limitations: It does not execute static analysis tools or inspect code automatically.
It focuses on general code quality, not security testing or performance profiling.
It gives review guidance, not framework-specific architecture rules.
It references a standards document that may not exist in every workspace.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist to names, functions, duplication, comments, and organization before merge.

use_cases.title: Coach Junior Developers
use_cases.description: Use guided questions to help teammates identify readability and design improvements themselves.

use_cases.title: Plan Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Identify large functions, deep nesting, repeated logic, and premature abstractions before changing code.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code using engineering fundamentals. Focus on naming, function size, duplication, organization, and comments.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Naming and Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this change for unclear names, generic variables, boolean naming, function verbs, and related code organization.

prompt_templates.title: Find Refactoring Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before a cleanup task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify refactoring opportunities in this code. Prioritize large functions, deep nesting, magic values, repeated logic, and unjustified abstractions.

prompt_templates.title: Lead a Socratic Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code as a mentor. Ask targeted questions about readability, responsibility boundaries, duplication, abstraction value, and SOLID tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A pull request has short variable names, repeated validation, and one long order-processing function.
output: The review calls out unclear naming and asks for descriptive variable names.
It suggests extracting repeated validation into a named helper.
It recommends splitting the long function by validation, calculation, persistence, and notification responsibilities.

output_examples.input: A developer created a reusable component with many options, but it is used once.
output: The review identifies premature abstraction as the main risk.
It asks whether the component has enough repeated use to justify configuration complexity.
It recommends a simpler implementation until the pattern appears multiple times.

output_examples.input: A class has many methods and directly creates several dependencies.
output: The review checks whether the class has more than one responsibility.
It raises dependency inversion concerns and asks where abstractions would reduce coupling.
It suggests separating unrelated behavior into focused collaborators.

best_practices: Use the checklist before merge, when changes are still easy to adjust.
Ask review questions that teach reasoning instead of only listing fixes.
Prioritize changes that improve readability, cohesion, and future maintenance.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every rule mechanically when the local codebase has stronger conventions.
Do not create abstractions before repeated use or clear responsibility boundaries exist.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for tests, security review, or performance measurement.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews naming, function design, duplication, organization, comments, documentation, and SOLID concerns.

faq.question: Does it run code analysis tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides prose guidance and review questions for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for junior developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Socratic questions that help juniors reason about quality tradeoffs.

faq.question: Can it replace project style guides?
faq.answer: No. Use project conventions first, then apply this checklist where guidance is missing.

faq.question: Does it cover security review?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on maintainability and readability, not threat modeling or vulnerability detection.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
